subject: infra.connect
name: 5G spectrum request for applications
position_end: Eleven lots across 700 MHz, 2.3 GHz and 3 GHz on a US$230m aggregate reserve and 15-year licences, amended in seven places by a consolidated response of 2026-07-31; no award made
note: whether the dominant operator applied, and at what price, is not established

subject: infra.connect
name: Annual fibre cuts
position_start: About 400 cuts a year in the early fibre-deployment years, undated
position_end: Over 8,000 cuts a year, with one sabotage and roadworks episode disrupting 157 sites
note: the earlier baseline is an undated early-years figure, not a 2025 measurement

subject: infra.connect
name: Cell-site build for 2026
position_start: 223 new sites a year on the ten-year average
position_end: 1,150 new sites planned for 2026 across two operators
note: no delivery figure against the 1,150 has been published as at 2026-08-05

subject: infra.connect
name: Dig Once policy
position_end: Draft framework finalised with the roads ministry and implementation targeted for the third quarter of 2026; no cabinet decision, instrument or commencement on record
note: claimed to cut fibre rollout cost by up to 60%

subject: infra.connect
name: Ghana-Burkina Faso frequency coordination agreement
position_end: Coordination agreement finalised with agreed cross-border signal-strength thresholds, in response to consumer interference complaints
note: nothing on file since on the thresholds set or compliance with them

subject: infra.connect
name: Internet exchange points
position_end: The Accra exchange past 200 Gbps, but three exchanges barely overlap: only 4 of 39 connected networks peer at all three, so most local traffic still transits abroad
note: the fragmentation is the finding rather than the traffic figure: an exchange's value is the traffic it keeps local, and three partly-overlapping exchanges keep less of it than one

subject: infra.connect
name: MTN Ghana capital expenditure
position_end: GHS 2,100.4m combined capital expenditure, down 36.3% on a restated GHS 3,298.7m, with intensity falling from 29.1% to 14.0%
note: roughly US$185m at the report's own June 2026 rate, against a stated US$380m 2026 tranche

subject: infra.connect
name: MTN Ghana capital programme
position_end: US$1.1bn equivalent over 2026 to 2028, with a first tranche of US$380m for 2026
note: the US$1bn figure of July 2026 is a restatement of the retired five-year pledge, not a second programme

subject: infra.connect
name: NGIC exclusive wholesale 5G licence
position_start: Sole licensed wholesale 5G operator, having already missed its June 2025 launch deadline
position_end: Exclusivity deleted by regulator amendment under the licence and the Electronic Communications Act; the rest of the licence and the spectrum assignment retained
note: the objection was heard and overruled on the record

subject: infra.connect
name: Register of authorised internet service providers
milestone: Register as at the second quarter of 2025
position_end: 78 authorised internet and public-data providers of which 42 are operational and 36 are not, with 35 of the 73 companies in the main internet and public-data class not operational and the single authorised rural provider itself not operational
note: an authorisation runs five years and recent authorisation dates sit against dormant entries, so the dormancy is a licensing backlog rather than lapsed incumbents

subject: infra.connect
name: Regulator quarterly telecom statistics
status: Implemented, published about eight months in arrears
position_start: The July to September 2024 bulletin the latest issue, published about eight months after the quarter
position_end: Still the latest issue held; it records 38.47m mobile voice subscriptions at 116.84% penetration, 25.56m mobile data subscriptions, one operator on 75.09% of the market and fixed broadband down 6.83% in the quarter to 216,143
note: the penetration rate exceeds 100% because it counts subscriptions, not people

subject: infra.connect
name: Rural coverage schedule for the dominant operator
milestone: Rewritten from licence-relative years to fixed dates
position_end: 40% of the rural population by 2029-12-01, 60% by 2032-12-01 and 80% by 2035-12-01, technology-neutral and non-retrospective
note: rewritten so that buying spectrum does not accelerate an existing commitment

subject: infra.connect
name: Satellite internet subscriptions
position_end: 15,384 in the second quarter of 2025, from 2,666 before satellite licensing
note: no Ghanaian satellite-subscription figure published for any quarter after mid-2025

subject: infra.connect
name: Satellite licensing framework
position_start: Licensed and operating, framework in force
position_end: 29 satellite licences issued, eleven of them last-mile; nothing published on the framework since

subject: infra.connect
name: Seventy per cent population coverage obligation
position_end: A licence condition on every 5G licensee to reach 70% of the total population on or before 2027-03-06 against the 2021 census, with a 90%-of-locality verification rule, confirmed band- and technology-neutral
note: the regulator concedes an incumbent meets it in substantial part from existing deployment

subject: infra.connect
name: Shared 5G wholesale network
position_start: Licensed but not launched, with a June 2025 launch deadline missed
position_end: Ghana's first shared 5G wholesale network live, its operator demoted from sole wholesaler to one participant

subject: infra.connect
name: Significant-market-power spectrum premium
milestone: Recharacterised in writing as a price, not a remedy
position_end: A 40% uplift on the dominant operator's 700 MHz and 3 GHz reserve prices, applied to the reserve only and not to bid ranking, with the regulator declining to publish its valuation model during a live assignment
note: stated to depend on no finding of contravention

subject: infra.connect
name: Submarine carrier services authorisation
position_end: Unchanged; a five-year renewable authorisation granted under section 3(c) of the National Communications Authority Act 2008, charging an annual regulatory fee of 1% of revenue, lapsing if not operated within two years, requiring not less than three years' notice of non-renewal, and obliging the holder to retain charging and financial data for six years and regulatory returns for two
note: a different object from the cable landing licence: it permits consortium members to sell capacity directly to users; the document held is the template, with the grantee left blank

subject: infra.connect
name: Transfer of the country-code domain to state control
position_start: Privately managed since 1996; no transfer proposed
position_end: Transfer to a state domain registry announced, with automatic assignment to newly registered businesses; no instrument, date or transfer step on record
sources: 2026-01-22 Ghana to take state control of .GH domain to strengthen digital identity

subject: infra.store
name: Africa Data Centres Accra facility
milestone: No dated status since the 2023 announcement
position_start: Announced at 10 MW initial capacity expandable to 30 MW on about US$100m of equity and development finance, construction due 2024
position_end: Unchanged; the first phase was due within 12 to 18 months of a 2024 start and no operational date, delay or cancellation is on file
note: the whole record is a 2023 press release

subject: infra.store
name: Agility Logistics Park data-centre campus
milestone: Listed among Africa's largest facilities, July 2026
position_end: 30 MW of committed IT capacity, designed for expansion to 150 MW
note: the country's largest facility by committed capacity, known only from a regional trade round-up with no Ghanaian primary

subject: infra.store
name: Commercial data-centre live IT load
position_end: About 4.8 MW of live critical IT load across 8 to 10 commercial facilities in 2024, against 7 MW in construction, about 60% occupancy and about US$12m of annual commercial revenue
note: Xalam Analytics' own modelled estimates for 2024, written for the EU digital investment facility, cited as such and not absorbed as official statistics

subject: infra.store
name: Digital Realty Accra data centre
position_end: Commissioned at up to 1.7 MW IT load and 500 racks, carrier-neutral and connected to a subsea landing
sources: 2025-11-04 Digital Realty Expands African Footprint With New Data Center in Ghana (ACR2)|2025-10-31-digital-realty-opens-accra-data-center-graphic
note: the two held accounts date it a month apart

subject: infra.store
name: National AI Compute Centre
position_end: US$250m announced by the President at the 2026-04-24 strategy launch, the larger of two dollar commitments totalling US$270m made that day; no site, operator, procurement route or date
note: a UNESCO official called unfunded, unexecuted AI strategies shell documents from the same platform; clarified 2026-08-05 - the US$270m is not the strategy's envelope but this US$250m plus a separate US$20m implementation allocation, and neither is the strategy's own GHS 5bn National AI Fund

subject: infra.store
name: National Data Centre
milestone: Modernisation stated at the AI summit
position_end: Being modernised to support AI workloads; no capacity, location, cost, contractor or timetable stated
note: one sentence in one source is the entire holding on the state's own data centre

subject: infra.energy
name: Data-centre power arrangements
position_end: No power purchase, tariff or on-site generation arrangement is published for any named Ghanaian facility; an analyst brief puts national installed capacity at about 6 GW of which roughly half reaches the end user, electricity at about US$0.12 per kWh and independent producers at more than 60% of capacity (2024 estimates)
note: the country-level power figures are an analyst's modelled estimates; nothing facility-specific is published

subject: infra.capacity
name: Submarine cable inventory
position_end: The regulator names five submarine cable providers - SAT-3, MainOne, WASC, Glo and ACE - on an undated page resting the licence on section 3(8) of the Electronic Communications Act 2008; an analyst brief counts six cables landing at Accra and about 2.5 Tbps of international capacity in use (2024 estimate)
note: the regulator's list carries no date and predates later landings; the six-cable count is an analyst's, not the regulator's

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Commercial AI-driven security operations centre
position_start: Operating from May 2025 as a commercial AI-driven security and digital-forensics centre
position_end: Unchanged; no client count, throughput or incident figure published since launch
note: the largest-in-Africa claim is the operator's own

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Community media cyber capability project
position_end: Czech-funded and implemented with the cyber-security authority and a digital-transformation centre, training about 60 media houses and more than 100 journalists in Accra through August 2026 and in Kumasi in September, and certifying those who complete every session and file a report into a proposed cyber-security press corps
note: budget not published; the press corps is proposed rather than constituted

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Critical information infrastructure designation
position_end: The communications minister says all central-bank-licensed entities will soon be designated critical information infrastructure; no instrument, date or designation list published

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cross-network mobile-money fraud monitoring
milestone: The dominant operator says it is working toward it
position_end: A centralised real-time layer able to block suspicious transfers as they move between networks, described as under discussion and nothing built
note: no operator, funder or timetable named

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cybersecurity Act 2020
position_start: In force as the cybersecurity statute, text not held
position_end: Unchanged; the text is now held - it establishes the Cyber Security Authority and a Cybersecurity Fund, provides for designation, registration and compliance audit of critical information infrastructure, and licenses cybersecurity service providers
note: the Act provides for licensing and accreditation of cybersecurity service providers; no licence register, designation list or enforcement record is held

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cybersecurity Act licensing enforcement
position_end: The Cyber Security Authority fined the Office of the Registrar of Companies and a service provider a combined GH¢360,000 for breaches of the Cybersecurity Act 2020 licensing requirements — GH¢240,000 against the Registrar in two penalties of GH¢120,000 for engaging an unlicensed cybersecurity service provider, and GH¢120,000 against the provider for operating without a licence
note: the base holds no prior published penalty under the Act, so this is the first enforcement on record rather than a series

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Financial Industry Security Operations Centre
milestone: Full fintech onboarding still an open recommendation
position_end: Expansion to all financial institutions including fintechs and microfinance announced in March 2026; four months later a digital-economy forum still lists complete onboarding as a recommendation
note: the same body is named two ways across the two accounts

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Joint Cyber Security Committee
milestone: Named as the apex coordination mechanism
position_end: Eighteen institutions, chaired by the cyber-security authority
note: no terms of reference, membership list, meeting cadence or output held

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National computer emergency response team
position_start: Operating as a unit of the cyber-security authority
position_end: Unchanged; a 24-hour incident-response service with a constituency of eight sectoral response teams and the general public, affiliated to the Budapest Convention
note: the profile is five years old and records its own policies as under review; no incident statistics or annual report is held

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Mobile money interoperability
position_start: Instant-pay value of GH¢120.1bn in 2023, with the interoperable share of the market not stated
position_end: 33.5m transactions worth GH¢6.2bn in June 2026, about 1.3% of total mobile-money value
sources: 2026-07-30-myjoyonline-mobile-money-transactions-june-2026-bog-data|2026-02-05 Ghana Mobile Money Interoperability Nearly Doubles in 2025
note: the share, not the volume, is the measure of interoperability

subject: dpi.id
name: Biometric SIM re-registration
milestone: Announced for the first quarter of 2026; timetable still unannounced
position_start: SIM registration moved fully online from June 2025
position_end: A fresh nationwide biometric drive still not begun, with the 2021 to 2023 registration declared invalid and the 2022 biometrics confirmed never authenticated against the identity database
note: liveness detection and 80% self-service are specified, with no start date on file

subject: dpi.id
name: Electronic number plate system (DVLA)
milestone: Enabling Legislative Instrument in force 28 May 2026; pilot stated for August 2026
position_end: Pilot stated to begin in August 2026 with nationwide rollout from January 2027, Cabinet having approved it and the Legislative Instrument in force since 28 May 2026 after a court challenge and parliamentary recess delayed it; the plates raise aluminium content from about 30% to 70%. No pilot size, cost or data-retention rule published
note: Dates and specification are the licensing authority's own; no procurement document is held.

subject: dpi.id
name: Ghana Card
milestone: Backlog of 640,000 cards cleared and distributed by September 2025
position_start: About 18m adults registered, with a printed-card backlog outstanding and applications moved online
position_end: 19.2m registered aged 15 and over, 262 institutions integrated, instant issuance nationwide and eleven overseas missions
sources: 2026-05-22-nia-clears-640000-backlog-diaspora-myjoy|2025-09-13 NIA clears Ghana Card backlog, issues instant card nationwide
note: the institutions-integrated count moved from 95 in September 2025 to 262 in early 2026

subject: dpi.id
name: Ghana Card as sole banking identity
position_end: Primary and sole identity document for financial onboarding at all regulated institutions, with biometric and liveness checks
sources: 2026-01-11 Ghana Card mandatory for banking and digital transactions - BoG

subject: dpi.id
name: Ghana Card enrolment for children aged 6 to 14
position_start: A plan announced to capture 7m under-fifteens and 3m diaspora
position_end: 3.1m children targeted, phased at 21 days per region, run jointly with the health insurance authority

subject: dpi.id
name: Ghana Card payment functionality
milestone: Claim denied by the issuing authority 2026-04-08
position_end: Still does not exist; the authority stated on 2026-04-08 that the card 'has not been activated for financial transaction purposes at this time'
sources: 2026-04-08-no-financial-transactions-with-ghana-card-yet-says-nia|2026-04-01 RETRACTION Ghana's National ID cards can now make payments
note: Reconciled 2026-08-05: not a contradiction but erroneous trade reporting, retracted. Reports of an activated card wallet reachable through MyCitizens and a *402# short code circulated 1-6 April 2026; the National Identification Authority denied them in a press release of 2026-04-08 signed by Williams Ampomah Emmanuel Darlas, Head of Corporate Affairs, quoted at length by Graphic, Citi Newsroom, MyJoyOnline and Pulse. The authority acknowledged high-level discussions on future integration and stated they 'remain inconclusive as of the time of this release'.

subject: dpi.id
name: Ghana Card photocopy ban and verification service
position_end: A three-month transition from 27 July to 2 November 2026 for banks, telecoms operators, hospitals, schools, insurers and agencies, with a sanctions ladder to suspension of verification access and licence withdrawal
note: verification tied to SIM registration is explicitly excluded, with no timetable announced

subject: dpi.id
name: National Identity Register Amendment Regulations 2026
milestone: In force 2026-06-09, signed 2 March and gazetted 27 March
position_start: Did not exist; the 2012 regulations as amended in 2018 were the standing rules
position_end: Biometric-only verification is law, visual inspection and photocopying are barred, and penalties run to 2,000 penalty units for an organisation
note: the gazetted artefact is an image scan with no text layer, so the regulation is not machine-readable

subject: dpi.id
name: Paid 24-hour identity service centre
position_end: A paid tier operating around the clock, all services attracting approved charges, the first of several planned nationwide
note: no fee schedule published and no queue baseline for the free centres it differentiates from

subject: dpi.pay
name: Active mobile money users, dominant operator
position_end: 19.3m at 31 December 2025 against 18.3m at 30 June 2026, with neither source stating the definition

subject: dpi.pay
name: Central bank digital currency pilot
milestone: Governor states the project is not abandoned
position_end: Pilot stage with the focus pivoted to cross-border settlement for sub-regional trade; no rollout date

subject: dpi.pay
name: Digital credit service provider regime
milestone: Enforcement opened after the 30 June 2026 deadline elapsed
position_end: A September 2025 directive in force from 1 November 2025, with applications from that month, the deadline elapsed and twenty unlicensed apps named on 2026-08-03
note: the notice that set the deadline is not held

subject: dpi.pay
name: Electronic money issuer licence revocation
milestone: Revoked 2026-07-14 under the Payment Systems and Services Act
position_start: A licensed dedicated electronic money issuer and development-finance investee
position_end: Licence revoked for electronic money not fully cash-backed, with premises access restricted by the central bank and police

subject: dpi.pay
name: Mobile money subsidiary separation
milestone: Structural separation completed in the first quarter of 2026
position_end: The mobile-money subsidiary files its own condensed statements inside the parent's report and declared its own interim dividend
note: the statutory basis is stated only by the secondary account

subject: dpi.pay
name: Mobile money transaction value
milestone: Central bank monthly data for June 2026
position_start: 6.81bn transactions worth GH¢1.92tn in the full year 2023
position_end: GH¢492.9bn on 954m transactions in June 2026 alone, up about 52% on June 2025
sources: 2026-07-30-myjoyonline-mobile-money-transactions-june-2026-bog-data|2024-01-01 Payment Systems Oversight Annual Report 2023 (Bank of Ghana)

subject: dpi.pay
name: National Virtual Asset Literacy Initiative (NaVALI)
position_end: Ashanti Regional phase of a nationwide virtual-asset education campaign led by the central bank and the securities regulator, anchored on a co-authored National Virtual Assets Education Manual and delivered in schools, markets and churches, described as a template for national rollout; no funding, timetable or nationwide launch date stated
note: awareness arm of the Virtual Asset Service Providers Act 2025 (row GHA-gov.legislate-virtual-asset-service-providers-act-2025); no nationwide date stated

subject: dpi.pay
name: Pan-African payment system participation
milestone: A state-majority bank confirmed as designated national gateway
position_start: A fintech-routed connection live under a six-month central-bank pilot
position_end: National gateway designated, a second bank live in-app, and a naira corridor from February 2026
sources: 2026-07-28-gcb-bank-papss-partnership|2026-07-30-prudential-bank-papss-mobile-graphic|2025-06-23 Onafriq and PAPSS launch cross-border payments in Ghana
note: nothing quantified: no volumes, tariff, corridor list or designation date

subject: dpi.pay
name: Register of licensed digital credit providers
milestone: Undertaken in July 2026 in due course, no date given
position_end: Still unpublished, with a twenty-name blacklist of unlicensed apps published instead
note: a borrower can check twenty names and cannot check whether the twenty-first is licensed

subject: dpi.pay
name: Registered and active mobile-money wallets
milestone: Central bank monthly data for June 2026
position_end: 84.6m registered and 26.4m active at 90 days in June 2026, with wallet float at a record GH¢40bn from GH¢28.9bn, and one million registered agents of whom 546,000 are active
note: the inclusion figure is 26.4m active, under a third of registered wallets

subject: dpi.pay
name: Renminbi settlement access
position_end: Direct settlement in renminbi from cedi accounts, in real time or batch, without correspondent-bank intermediation

subject: dpi.registry
name: Births and deaths registry digitisation
position_start: Decentralised printing across 470 offices in 261 districts with electronically signed certificates, and 881,000 copies needed to clear the backlog
position_end: Unchanged; nothing dated since
note: whether the backlog cleared is not established

subject: dpi.registry
name: Business registration platform
milestone: In pilot, launch given only as the coming months
position_end: End-to-end filing from name search to certification with no physical submission, integrating with national identification for verification
note: a companion beneficial-ownership verification service pilots with banks on a subscription basis

subject: dpi.registry
name: Land cadastre digitalisation
position_start: A fit-for-purpose cadastre programme expected to commence in 2023
position_end: Unchanged; no dated progress on file
sources: 2023-01-01 Digitalization of Land Administration in Ghana (Lands Commission)
note: the date is a year-precision proxy off an undated slide deck

subject: dpi.registry
name: Land Use Planning and Management Information System
position_end: Being redeveloped into a web-based platform for spatial planning, development control and street addressing, with data sharing and interoperability against existing government systems consulted on; carried inside a spatial-planning sub-programme appropriated GHS 36,454,968 for 2026, from which no digital share is separable
note: the redevelopment is stated to run with GIZ support, which is not costed in the estimates; no launch date, contractor or district count is published

subject: dpi.mis
name: Health management information system
position_end: Rollout directed and a vendor engaged; no completion, facility count or coverage figure held since
note: replaces a failed US$77m contract with about 15m records reconstructed

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Cross-border electronic commerce tax platform
position_end: Piloted April 2026 with a named private operator and a first-full-year projection of GH¢3.2bn, which is a projection and not an outturn
note: model, total cost, duration and termination terms undisclosed

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Customs valuation AI system
milestone: Fully deployed from March 2026 after a January to February pilot
position_end: About 366,000 declarations analysed to 2026-07-17, 24% triggering more than one valuation risk indicator, with collections up 17.5% against a 6.3% rise in declared value
note: the figures are the finance ministry's own and unaudited, and importers have contested the rollout

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Electronic procurement system
milestone: The finance minister directed all state institutions onto it
position_end: Mandatory end-to-end electronic procurement with pre-disclosed evaluation criteria, integrated with the national payment system
note: the procurement authority's claim is substantial reduction, not elimination, of procurement corruption

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Fiscal electronic device policy
position_end: An advanced pilot under the 2018 fiscal-device Act, to be paired with a reward scheme, with a projection of GH¢7.2bn a year
note: unit cost and who ultimately bears it were not disclosed to Parliament

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Ghana.gov services portal
position_start: About 1,500 to 2,000 services live against a 16,000 target, with a redesign due in the fourth quarter of 2025
position_end: The redesign still not launched and no service count published since July 2025
note: the fourth-quarter 2025 relaunch target passed with nothing on file recording delivery

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Second public sector reform strategy
milestone: Validated at a national stakeholder workshop 2026-07-30
position_end: Draft on seven pillars, 27 programmes and 135 activities with the identity credential as the spine, expected at cabinet and Parliament by end-2026
note: phase-one lessons are stated candidly: delayed fund releases, fragmented coordination, weak performance management

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Tax Modernisation Master Plan
position_end: A Korean-backed plan covering income tax, value-added tax, tax administration and electronic tax administration; no cost, timetable or implementing schedule is published
note: prepared with a Korean development agency and its public-finance institute; artificial intelligence is already in service on customs valuation, which is a separate row on this ledger

subject: gov.legislate
name: Data Exchange Act
position_end: Named by the ministry as a statute distinct from harmonisation, carrying interoperability and inter-agency sharing, with no draft or timetable

subject: gov.legislate
name: Data Harmonisation Bill
position_start: Named as a forthcoming Act the new board must support, with no draft
position_end: Consulted on and still a bill, renamed an Act in the July 2026 AI plan, not laid before Parliament
note: the information technology agency would be both regulator and technical enforcer of the standards

subject: gov.legislate
name: Digital banking framework
position_end: Framework and comprehensive draft guidelines complete, awaiting stakeholder consultation before implementation, with no date

subject: gov.legislate
name: Digital Economy and Innovation Development Fund Bill
position_end: Under legislative review, converting the universal-access fund into a wider digital-infrastructure, innovation and skills fund; levy rate, governance structure and the fate of the rural-access earmark all unestablished
note: the draft text is not published by the ministry under any heading

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic Communications Act 2008
position_start: In force as the licensing statute for electronic communications
position_end: Unchanged; the statute under which 5G licences and submarine-cable landings are granted, which establishes the universal-access fund and sources it from contributions stipulated in each licence rather than from any rate set in the Act
note: five of the fund's ten trustees are elected by the Industry Forum, seating the levy-payers on the board that spends the levy

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic Transactions Bill 2025
milestone: Draft published on the ministry's site, dated 2025-10-20
position_start: The 2008 electronic transactions Act as the standing baseline, with no replacement on record
position_end: A draft that would mandate age verification for child-accessible services, ban targeted advertising to children and impose risk assessments and semi-annual transparency reports on very large platforms
sources: 2026-01-11 The Year of the Teeth Data Protection in Africa Roundup, 2025, Projections for 2026
note: the prior status describes the 2008 Act it would replace, not the bill

subject: gov.legislate
name: Emerging Technologies Bill
milestone: To be laid before Parliament in 2026
position_end: A draft that would create an emerging-technologies agency for cross-functional compliance across artificial intelligence, blockchain, connected devices, cloud and quantum, with voluntary startup registration
sources: 2026-01-11 The Year of the Teeth Data Protection in Africa Roundup, 2025, Projections for 2026
note: the chosen vehicle instead of a standalone AI act; no text held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Identity agency Act amendment
position_end: Would place the identity agency permanently under the interior ministry and grant security agencies defined access to the biometric citizen database
note: the base carries nothing after August 2025 despite the civil-liberties objections it drew

subject: gov.legislate
name: Information technology agency bill
position_end: A draft that would overhaul the 2008 law, license every technology business, certify professionals, regulate artificial intelligence and blockchain and levy 1% on services, and split the agency's regulatory and commercial arms
note: the minister's answer to critics is that detail comes in a later legislative instrument

subject: gov.legislate
name: Innovation and Startup Bill
position_start: A draft startup law under development, with no text
position_end: Still forthcoming, now tied to a national financial-technology fund it would give a legal base and eligibility criteria, with no draft published and none laid
sources: 2026-07-07 Ghana and UNDP Strengthen Partnership on Digital Transformation Projects
note: recorded as under development since at least September 2024 with no published step in between

subject: gov.legislate
name: Right to Information Act 2019 (Act 989)
milestone: 254 public bodies fined under section 77(1), 5 August 2026
position_end: In force and enforced: the Right to Information Commission fined 254 public bodies GHS 20,000 each for failing to file their mandatory 2025 annual reports, after reminders published in the Gazette; no collection figure, appeal outcome or compliance rate published
note: The sanction count is the Commission's own; whether the fines were paid is not established.

subject: gov.legislate
name: SIM re-registration legislative instrument
position_end: Still not laid on file, with the first-quarter 2026 start date passed and a later-in-2026 rollout restated in February
note: no baseline at the window's opening, but a stated target has passed undelivered

subject: gov.legislate
name: Virtual Asset Service Providers Act 2025
position_start: No statute, with more than 3 million virtual-asset users and over 100 service providers recorded in a July 2025 registration exercise, and regulated institutions directed not to facilitate virtual-asset activity at all
position_end: In force on the regulator's account, risk-based and technology-neutral with capital adequacy, client-asset custody and anti-money-laundering duties, supervision split between the central bank and the securities regulator by activity, licensing attaching to the service rather than to holding, virtual assets excluded from deposit protection and from any statutory compensation fund and barred from invoicing, pricing and wages, transition arrangements for existing operators, and the licensing requirements still being built
note: the Act's gazetted text is not held, so every characterisation is the central bank's own; the November 2025 policy position records that prohibition was ruled out on FATF's 2015 guidance

subject: gov.policy
name: National AI health policy
position_end: A health ministry draft anchored on Article 34(2) of the 1992 Constitution, covering approval, procurement, validation, human oversight, monitoring, evaluation and accountability across public and private facilities, and barring patient data from leaving the country without safeguards; not adopted, and no text published
note: the ministry's own stakeholder survey reports 44% of respondents already using or piloting AI and 88% concerned about patient data privacy (2026-08-05); the draft names unreliable electricity and internet connectivity among four risks requiring attention before scale

subject: gov.policy
name: National AI implementation plan
position_end: Being built with UN partners on measurable annual milestones over a decade, framed against the risk of a shelf document
note: no plan text, publication date or milestone list on file

subject: gov.policy
name: National AI Strategy 2023-2033
position_start: In preparation with regional and donor partners, not approved or funded
position_end: Approved and launched, with the text held from 2026-08-05; a ten-year implementation plan with annual milestones announced 2026-07-29, a National AI Fund of GHS 5bn (2025-2030) scaling to GHS 15bn (2030-2035) in the strategy, and US$250m plus US$20m announced separately at the launch
sources: 2026-04-24-moc-ghana-launches-national-ai-strategy|2026-04-25-president-unveils-270m-national-ai-strategy-graphic|2026-04-03 Ghana approves $250M AI Hub & National AI Strategy|2026-07-30-ghana-10-year-ai-implementation-roadmap
note: the text is held from 2026-08-05 and gives the range as 2025-2035, not the 2023-2033 this row is named for; the US$270m is not the strategy's own envelope but two dollar commitments announced at the 2026-04-24 launch - US$250m for a national AI computing centre and US$20m for short-to-medium-term implementation - while the strategy's own instrument is a National AI Fund of GHS 5bn scaling to GHS 15bn

subject: gov.policy
name: National Data Strategy
position_end: No adoption, publication or implementation step on file in the two years since validation
sources: 2024-07-02 Ghana develops its National Data Strategy with Smart Africa and Team Europe
note: European partners enabled it, which makes the silence since 2024 the finding

subject: gov.policy
name: Responsible AI oversight body
milestone: Provided for at the strategy launch, within the first year
position_start: Proposed at a national consultation, with no legal basis or timetable
position_end: Provided for in the launched strategy, with no establishing instrument, budget or staff sixteen months after first proposal
sources: 2026-04-25-president-unveils-270m-national-ai-strategy-graphic|2026-02-28-ai-strategy-knust-leadership-myjoy|2026-04-03 Ghana approves $250M AI Hub & National AI Strategy
note: sources differ on whether this is one body or an authority plus a ministry office

subject: gov.regional
name: Anti-IFFs Policy Tracker (Ghana)
milestone: AU Ministerial Declaration (Abidjan, 20-24 Jul 2026) endorses continental roll-out from the six-country pilot including Ghana
position_end: Piloted in Ghana over eighteen months alongside Cote d'Ivoire, Liberia, Namibia, Uganda and Zambia, with UNECA support; Ghana's finance ministry reports the Tracker contributed to recovering millions of dollars in revenue; AU now endorses continental roll-out from diagnostic pilot to standing self-assessment instrument; no Ghana-specific score, findings or reform list published

subject: gov.regional
name: Digital Policy Alert / St Gallen Endowment partnership
milestone: Announced at an Accra stakeholder workshop, 2026-08-10
position_end: Partnership between the communications ministry (MoCDTI) and Digital Policy Alert, with the St Gallen Endowment for Prosperity through Trade, bringing DPA's digital-policy intelligence platform and AI-assisted regulatory-analysis tools to the National AI Strategy, data-governance work and the One Million Coders Programme, framed around Ghana's AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol and WTO engagement; no funding, duration or deliverables stated

subject: gov.regional
name: Ghana-Rwanda fintech licence passporting memorandum
position_end: Still unpublished by either central bank as at 2026-07-30, so which licence categories are recognised and on what conditions is unestablished
note: bilateral and signed by the central bank, so a Ghanaian instrument rather than a bloc one

subject: gov.standards
name: Cyber and Information Security Directive 2026
position_start: An earlier directive in force, text and date not held
position_end: In force as the country's first comprehensive AI-governance framework for financial institutions, with cloud-security rules, proportionality by size and risk and mandatory board-level accountability
note: the governor states the industry was consulted before issue

subject: gov.standards
name: Government data exchange hub
position_start: Launched 2009 and stalled on funding and unclear mandates
position_end: Named again by the communications minister as a National Data Exchange Hub government plans to establish for standardised and interoperable sharing between institutions, with no design, cost or timetable stated
sources: 2024-01-01 Ghana national data exchange case study (Digital Impact Alliance)|2026-07-31-govt-committed-to-building-ai-ecosystem-to-create-jobs-promote-economic-growth
note: the statement does not say whether the hub revives the system launched in 2009 or replaces it; the interoperability legal base is being rebuilt through the harmonisation bill in parallel

subject: gov.protect
name: Data Protection Act 2012
position_start: In force as the sole general data-protection statute, with controllers and processors the regulated class
position_end: In force and unamended, with a draft replacement published during 2025 and not enacted
sources: 2026-02-27-minister-data-protection-foundation-techreview|2026-01-11 The Year of the Teeth Data Protection in Africa Roundup, 2025, Projections for 2026
note: reaches controllers and processors, not the data-broker layer an operator names as the leak

subject: gov.protect
name: Data Protection Commission
position_start: Operating under the 2012 Act, with a new governing board sworn in that day and tasked with a national data-governance framework
position_end: Operating, with 2026 declared a year of enforcement and a size-banded fee schedule in force from 2026-02-02
note: the baseline date and the swearing-in are the same day

subject: gov.protect
name: Data-protection enforcement actions
position_end: Still no fine, prosecution or registered-controller count published, twelve months on
note: the only quantities published are awareness ones

subject: gov.protect
name: Draft Data Protection Act 2025
position_end: A draft that would require domestic storage of data critical to national security, civil registration and sensitive personal data including children's, biometric, health and genetic data
sources: 2026-01-11 The Year of the Teeth Data Protection in Africa Roundup, 2025, Projections for 2026
note: known only from a third-party roundup; no draft text and no month within 2025

subject: gov.protect
name: United States health data-sharing agreement
position_end: Offered and refused: a five-year agreement that, on the data-protection regulator's account, covered not only health data sets but metadata, dashboards, reporting tools, data models and data dictionaries, gave ten United States entities access requiring no prior Ghanaian approval, required 25 years of citizens' health records, and settled disputes under United States law against US$109m subject to congressional appropriation
note: the terms are the regulator's executive director quoted by a state news agency, not a published text; the further reported demand to integrate the national identity database with American systems in real time is attributed by that report to another agency citing unnamed sources

subject: gov.protect
name: Upgrade of the data-protection regulator to an authority
position_start: Announced by the minister at the board swearing-in, with no bill
position_end: Announced, with no bill, no timetable and no further mention on file in twelve months

subject: include.divides
name: American-funded digital inclusion and connectivity programming
milestone: 83% of the agency's programmes cut, stated March 2025
position_end: Planned and running work slowed or stopped after the 2025 wind-down, with no replacement funder named
note: the multi-funder Women in the Digital Economy Fund lost its American component while the parts other funders backed continued; the account is an implementing partner's, and no figure for the Ghanaian share is stated

subject: include.divides
name: Community network licensing framework
milestone: The regulator floats an existing hotspot authorisation as a possible base
position_end: No dedicated regime exists; the regulator says an existing hotspot authorisation could found one, and its own register shows four such authorisations, each capped by rule at three administrative districts and all operational, against a single authorised rural provider that is not operational
note: a civil-society policy lead places four other African states ahead of Ghana on enabling frameworks

subject: include.divides
name: Fourth-generation coverage against usage
milestone: The minister's statement at a trade fair
position_end: Fourth-generation networks reach more than 90% of the population while actual usage runs below 60%, with many users still on feature phones
sources: 2026-03-05 Ghana strikes AI training deal with Chinese multinational amid $250m tech investment push
note: no later reading held; the gap is the ministry's own framing of the device-affordability problem

subject: include.divides
name: Household survey of digital access
milestone: Abridged report published 2020-11-02 on June 2019 fieldwork
position_start: A 2019 regulator household survey, with a biennial repeat stated as intent
position_end: No repeat round; 16.8% of households with internet access against 73.8% owning a television, 7.9% of people aged five and over owning a computer of any kind, and smartphone ownership at 58.4% urban against 28.1% rural
note: a 2022 survey wave published in October 2025 and a qualitative gender study published in February 2026 are the only later demand-side readings held

subject: include.divides
name: Rural telephony and digital inclusion project
position_end: Continuing, with the fund restating it as top priority and taking an upgraded mast design
note: the last disbursement figure held is 60.2% as at May 2022; no site count, coverage figure or completion date

subject: include.divides
name: Universal access fund
milestone: The draft development fund bill would convert it
position_end: Still operating as the universal-access fund with the rural telephony project its stated top priority, and slated for conversion
note: the base holds no levy receipts, accounts or disbursement figure at any date

subject: include.access
name: Cash-grant programme on mobile-money rails
milestone: GH¢485m paid in the first half of 2026
position_end: A full-year allocation of GH¢1.1bn, the highest since inception, with a recent cycle releasing about GH¢139m to roughly 350,580 households
sources: 2026-07-23-ghana-2026-mid-year-fiscal-policy-review-speech|2025-12-22 Government begins 99th cycle of LEAP cash-grant payments
note: the stated expansion to 400,000 households in 2026 has no delivery figure on file

subject: include.access
name: Unlimited fibre tariff
milestone: The minister announced the cut, effective the same day
position_start: GH¢987 per month for an unlimited 100 Mbit/s package
position_end: GH¢299 per month, with 300 Mbit/s at GH¢444 and 500 Mbit/s at GH¢999
note: a cut extracted by ministerial pressure on one operator, not a licensing change that lets others compete

subject: tech.ai
section: Artificial intelligence and the technology sector
name: Customs AI attributed revenue
milestone: Over GH¢300m claimed March to 17 July 2026
position_end: Monthly figures of GH¢73.44m, GH¢51.63m, GH¢72.5m, GH¢55.82m and GH¢35.17m to 17 July, the finance ministry's own and unaudited
note: the monthly series declines after March, unremarked in the source, and causal attribution is asserted rather than demonstrated

subject: tech.ai
section: Artificial intelligence and the technology sector
name: Disaster management AI chatbot
position_end: Owned by the national disaster management organisation, answering on floods, fires, storms, droughts, earthquakes, epidemics and localised hazards in several international and local languages and issuing automated responses during an emergency, with officers from ten regional offices trained online on 2026-06-04 and six regions still without an emergency operations centre
note: built under a UNESCO project funded by the Government of Japan; no cost, user count or availability figure is published, and connectivity was intermittent during the online training itself

subject: tech.ai
section: Artificial intelligence and the technology sector
name: Flood Intelligence Agent
milestone: Named as in development at a Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology lecture, reported 2026-08-10
position_end: In development; no launch date, scope or funding figure published
note: named alongside two live BigData Ghana deployments as a system still in development

subject: tech.ai
section: Artificial intelligence and the technology sector
name: Google Africa applied AI lab
position_end: Described by its sponsor as Africa's first applied AI lab, sited at an Accra community centre with research and venture partners; the first cohort is not yet selected
sources: 2026-07-01 Google Cloud Summit in Africa Highlights the Continent's Digital Transformation and Unveils New Agentic AI and Infrastructure Investments|2026-07-29-google-ouvre-les-candidatures-pour-l-africa-applied-ai-lab
note: no cohort size, funding figure or Ghana-specific spend disclosed

subject: tech.ai
section: Artificial intelligence and the technology sector
name: National AI Strategy document
milestone: Published December 2025 by the communications ministry
position_end: The Republic of Ghana National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025-2035, published by the Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations and dated December 2025, held in full
note: the text corrected two things the base carried from launch reporting - the range is 2025-2035 not 2023-2033, and the body proposed is a Responsible AI Authority not an Office - and it settles the National AI Fund at GHS 5bn scaling to GHS 15bn

subject: tech.industry
section: Artificial intelligence and the technology sector
name: Micro-enterprise tax platform
position_end: Nationwide commercial deployment with the revenue authority, targeting about 530,000 small enterprises onboarded in the first twelve months
note: targets and economics are the vendor's own projections, with no independent onboarding figure since launch

subject: tech.industry
section: Artificial intelligence and the technology sector
name: Mobile money intellectual-property claim
position_end: Live before the commercial division of the High Court, with the operator saying the claims are without merit and that it will contest fully; no monetary figure pleaded
note: the claimant dates its authorship claim to a 2007 commission and explains the delay by 2026 publication of verifiable scale figures

subject: tech.industry
section: Artificial intelligence and the technology sector
name: Technology sector contribution to output and employment
milestone: Satellite account issued for public comment November 2017
position_start: A single regulator-commissioned satellite account, with data ending in 2014
position_end: Unchanged; ICT gross value added of GHS 2,489.3m in 2014 and a share of gross domestic product falling in every year of the series, from 3.1% in 2010 to 2.2% in 2014
note: the study reports ICT gross value added exceeding the published Information and Communication sector total, which it calls a plausible underestimation; it carries no employment figure and was never repeated

subject: tech.innovate
section: Artificial intelligence and the technology sector
name: Assistive vision technology
milestone: In pilot with a disability association
position_start: A post-hackathon prototype from a 2024 competition
position_end: Two devices in pilot, smart glasses and an ultrasonic obstacle detector, at a target price of about GH¢2,000 and a 1,500-user target within a year

subject: tech.innovate
section: Artificial intelligence and the technology sector
name: Startup equity funding
position_end: US$41,225,000 across eight startups in 2025, seventh in Africa and 2.5% of the continental total
note: the same report calls the market in steady decline as a funding destination since 2022 despite the rise

subject: geopol.usa
section: Artificial intelligence and the technology sector
name: Google AI research and community centre
position_start: Operating, with a US$37m cumulative investment figure disclosed by the company
position_end: Unchanged; it hosts the new applied AI lab and no further Ghana investment figure has been published since
note: the figure is the company's own cumulative aggregate, not a new commitment

subject: geopol.eu
name: Ghana-EU digital instrument
milestone: Amended by Commission Implementing Decision C(2024)7502
position_start: A 2021 to 2027 programme with digital folded through three priority areas rather than given its own
position_end: Unchanged in shape; the EUR 203m for 2021 to 2024 is followed by EUR 136m for 2025 to 2027 supplied at the mid-term review, split between green growth for jobs EUR 42m, smart and sustainable cities EUR 45m, good governance and security EUR 40m and support measures EUR 9m, with digital again given no priority area of its own
sources: 2021-12-16-eu-ghana-multiannual-indicative-programme-2021-2027|2024-07-02 Ghana develops its National Data Strategy with Smart Africa and Team Europe|2024-01-01-eu-amending-decision-mip-2021-2027-sub-saharan-africa-annex-c2024-7502
note: the document's own diagnosis is that the information technology agency lacks both the technical capacity for integrated digital-government planning and the funding to implement the platforms government envisages; the amending decision carries no date in its text and is placed in 2024 by its decision number alone

subject: geopol.india
section: Artificial intelligence and the technology sector
name: Ghana-India technology cooperation instrument
milestone: No sources on file for this place and subject
position_end: Zero sources held
note: a bilateral memorandum, a line-of-credit record or an Indian vendor contract would settle it

subject: geopol.gulf
section: Artificial intelligence and the technology sector
name: Ghana-Gulf technology investment instrument
milestone: No sources on file for this place and subject
position_end: Zero sources held
note: a sovereign-fund agreement, or a data-centre or AI memorandum, would settle it

subject: capacity.literacy
name: National privacy awareness campaign
position_end: All sixteen regions, delivered in English plus five Ghanaian languages, scheduled to end September 2026
note: no reach figure, evaluation or extension statement held, and the campaign ends within two months of this report

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Revised basic-education curriculum
milestone: The curriculum council completed the revision; awaiting cabinet and Parliament
position_end: Announced not adopted, to go to the President, then cabinet, then Parliament
note: no adoption date, cost, device provision or teacher-training plan published

subject: capacity.training
name: Digital Parliaments Project Africa
milestone: Launched at a capacity-training event in the Parliament of Ghana
position_end: Launched by the POPVOX-DPP Foundation with the House Democracy Partnership; launch cohort of the parliaments of Ghana, Botswana and South Africa, the National Assemblies of the Gambia and Senegal, and the Pan-African Parliament; no funder, budget, duration or work programme stated

subject: capacity.training
name: Distance-learning loan for a local government institute
position_end: The completion date passed with nothing recorded, and the record itself flags indications of financial underperformance
note: the country announced sovereign default in December 2022

subject: capacity.training
name: Distance-learning loan for tertiary institutions
position_end: The expected completion date passed with no completion, disbursement or outturn statement on file
note: connects satellite campuses to fibre; borrowing terms unknown

subject: capacity.training
name: Education fund and UNESCO AI teacher training programme
position_end: A memorandum to train teachers and instructors in technical and vocational institutions in digital and AI skills, placed under UNESCO's Global Skills Academy and delivered through a three-month master-trainer cascade ending in examinations, with commercial partners named
note: no commitment amount, cohort size or funding split is published, so it carries no finance record

subject: capacity.training
name: Girls in ICT programme
milestone: A vendor agreed free AI training for 3,000 girls at a trade fair
position_start: A two-week residential model in coding, animation, web development, cybersecurity and basic computing, with about 18,000 girls and 1,800 teachers since 2012
position_end: An AI module added as the largest curriculum expansion to date, with completers transitioning into the coders programme
sources: 2026-03-05 Ghana strikes AI training deal with Chinese multinational amid $250m tech investment push
note: the 18,000 is cumulative since 2012, not an annual rate; no start date, cohort or delivery report five months on

subject: capacity.training
name: Korean youth leadership programme
position_end: 200 participants from Ghana, Nigeria, Cote d'Ivoire, Senegal and Cameroon across online training, in-country sessions at a public administration institute and a funded 14-day study visit to Korea for top performers, coupling public governance with AI-driven digital-government innovation
note: the donor's stated US$34m African governance-training footprint is undated and its Ghanaian or AI share is not disclosed

subject: capacity.training
name: One Million Coders Programme
milestone: A university embedded it in curriculum 2026-07-29
position_start: Launched April 2025 against a target of one million trained by 2030
position_end: The first tertiary institution embeds it permanently, with 2,500 laptops delivered and an AI feeder cohort routed into it
sources: 2026-07-29-university-of-ghana-embeds-coding-programme|2026-07-30-ghana-expands-one-million-coders-programme-with-2000-additional-laptops|2026-03-05 Ghana strikes AI training deal with Chinese multinational amid $250m tech investment push
note: no cumulative trained figure has ever been published

subject: capacity.training
name: Youth agency microdegree programme
position_end: Government-funded vendor-certified microdegrees in cloud, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and data analytics, taking 2,000 of the 3,000 places allocated to Africa, with 600 paid internships and a five-region pilot
note: programme cost not disclosed despite being fully government-funded

subject: capacity.research
name: Innovation centre at a public university
position_end: An advanced technology innovation centre with a foreign development agency, recorded as active
note: no progress or outturn report held at any date

subject: digital.localgov
name: Local government electronic services
position_end: Nothing held; the public-sector reform strategy names local government only as an integration target
note: a district service platform, or a local-government digitisation report, would settle it

subject: data.statistics
name: Governance Series survey
position_end: A six-monthly repeat panel run by the statistical service across all 16 regions, with its third wave published and its findings put by the Government Statistician to remedies that are digital ones, among them digitising public services and publishing official fees
note: the report text is not held; the wave figures come from the launch as reported

subject: data.statistics
name: Quarterly employment statistics
milestone: The finance minister asked the statistical service to develop a methodology
position_end: Still none published, with a methodology requested in July 2026 and no timetable

subject: data.open
name: National open-data instrument
milestone: No policy, portal, licence or inventory on file
position_end: The base carries no Ghanaian open-data policy, portal, licence or dataset inventory
note: a published policy or a live inventory would settle it

subject: data.satellite
name: Ghana Agricultural Information and Monitoring System
milestone: Named as a live deployment at a Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology lecture, reported 2026-08-10
position_end: Live spatial/agricultural data platform named by BigData Ghana's co-founder as one of three live deployments; no coverage, user or funding figure published

subject: data.satellite
name: National Forest Monitoring System and ForestTrace AI deforestation tracker
milestone: Named as a live deployment at a Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology lecture, reported 2026-08-10
position_end: Live national forest monitoring system paired with the ForestTrace AI deforestation tracker, built toward EU Deforestation Regulation compliance for cocoa and gold supply chains; no coverage or accuracy figure published

subject: finance.new
name: AI implementation fund
position_end: US$20m earmarked for short-to-medium-term implementation, with no appropriation, disbursement or managing body named
note: US$20m earmarked for short-to-medium-term implementation of the strategy, announced by the President at the 2026-04-24 launch and distinct from the National AI Fund. The separate National AI Fund now has a size, resolved 2026-08-05 against the strategy text: GHS 5bn seed over 2025-2030, scaling to GHS 15bn over 2030-2035, with a funding prioritisation committee. Carried in cedis because that is the announcing party's currency; it is not a conversion of, and does not sum with, the US$20m or the US$250m. No appropriation, disbursement or managing body is named for any of the three.

subject: finance.new
name: Digital acceleration project
milestone: US$200m, effective June 2023, running to June 2027
position_start: US$200m committed, with the services portal to add about 16,000 services in the fourth quarter of 2025
position_end: Still named as a pillar of the digital agenda; the portal target has no delivery statement on file, and US$18.3m had been disbursed
note: the disbursement figure carries no date of its own in the record

subject: finance.new
name: Electronic road toll concession
milestone: Parliament approved a 20-year PPP toll concession, 2026-07-31
position_start: Tolls suspended since November 2021; no PPP concession
position_end: 20-year PPP between the Ministry of Roads and Highways and an SPV to be established by Rock Africa Limited, for nationwide fully electronic toll collection; no concession value, revenue split, corridor count, build timetable or collection technology stated

subject: finance.new
name: National financial-technology fund
milestone: Ministerial update to a development partner 2026-07-07
position_end: To be aligned with a forthcoming innovation and startup framework that would set eligibility and give the fund a legal basis
sources: 2026-07-07 Ghana and UNDP Strengthen Partnership on Digital Transformation Projects
note: no size, source of funds or date

subject: finance.budget
name: Domestic digital-transformation appropriation
position_end: GHS 729,947,850 for ICT Infrastructure, Regulation and Capacity Building, of which GHS 591,947,850 is domestically funded, and GHS 100,000,000 for ICT Capacity Development, under the communications ministry's 2026 vote; the domestic figure resolves to GHS 536,745,448 for the information technology agency, GHS 25,346,198 for the cyber-security authority, GHS 17,308,560 for the ICT capacity centre, GHS 9,720,400 for the data-protection regulator and GHS 2,827,244 for the domain registry
note: the data-protection regulator's GHS 9,720,400 is entirely its own internally generated funds, with no Consolidated Fund allocation; the same Act appropriates GHS 148,820,843 for passport administration and GHS 20,413,271 for the Right to Information Commission, and the mid-year fiscal review names none of these lines

subject: finance.budget
name: Multi-year commitment for three revenue platforms
milestone: Parliament adopted the finance committee reports 2026-07-28
position_end: Approved with published benefit projections and no disclosed cost, contract duration or termination terms
note: the opposition alleges the cross-border operator takes up to 3% of collections, which it estimates at about GH¢690m a year
